statement: Tarnwick Industrial Group reported total revenue of $4,187.3 million for fiscal year 2025 (the year ended 30 September 2025).
Tarnwick Industrial Group's net income attributable to shareholders for fiscal year 2025 was $276.4 million.
Tarnwick Industrial Group's board declared a final dividend of $0.37 per share for fiscal year 2025, payable on 18 December 2025.
Tarnwick Industrial Group had 11,462 full-time employees as of 30 September 2025.
The external auditor of Tarnwick Industrial Group for fiscal year 2025 was Marlowe & Finch LLP.
Tarnwick Industrial Group's board authorized a share repurchase program of up to $225 million, expiring on 31 March 2027.
Tarnwick Industrial Group's approved capital expenditure budget for fiscal year 2026 is $418 million.
The senior notes due 2031 issued by Tarnwick Industrial Group carry a fixed coupon of 5.375% per year.

Tarnwick Industrial Group's gross margin fell to 27.9% in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 from 29.4% a year earlier, which management attributed to a six-week production stoppage at the Dunmarrow plant after a coolant system failure.

In November 2025 Tarnwick Industrial Group agreed to acquire Corvane Dynamics for $734 million, paid 60% in cash and 40% in newly issued Tarnwick shares, with closing expected in the second quarter of fiscal 2026 subject to approval from the Eastmark Competition Authority.
Tarnwick Industrial Group recorded a restructuring charge of $48.6 million in fiscal 2025 for closing the Halbrook foundry, a closure that eliminated 640 jobs.
Tarnwick Industrial Group recognized a goodwill impairment of $91.2 million on its Aquaflow Controls reporting unit in fiscal 2025, citing a lower forecast for municipal water-meter orders.

Tarnwick Industrial Group's $750 million revolving credit facility matures on 14 March 2030, was undrawn at the end of fiscal 2025, and requires the company to keep its net leverage ratio at or below 3.25 times.
Tarnwick CEO Ingrid Vasterholm's fiscal 2025 annual bonus was paid at 142% of target, with free cash flow carrying the largest weighting (40%) among the bonus metrics.

Tarnwick Industrial Group is the defendant in the class action Hallwick v. Tarnwick, filed in the Meridian District Court, which alleges that inventory values were misstated; the company has set aside a reserve of $17.5 million for it.

Tarnwick Chief Financial Officer Odalys Brennmark previously served as CFO of Corvane Dynamics until 2022, and for that reason she recused herself from the board vote approving the Corvane acquisition.
The Precision Components segment, which owns the Dunmarrow plant, was the only one of Tarnwick Industrial Group's three segments whose revenue declined in fiscal 2025.

Audit Committee chair Priyanka Delacroix-Oyelaran was formerly a partner at Marlowe & Finch LLP, the company's external auditor, and the committee confirmed that the required five-year cooling-off period since she left the firm had elapsed.

Proceeds from Tarnwick's 5.375% senior notes due 2031 were used to repay in full the $380 million Brandt-Lyle term loan, which had originally financed the 2022 purchase of the Aquaflow Controls business.
The largest single allocation in Tarnwick's fiscal 2026 capital expenditure plan, $142 million, is for a new plant in Kessendal that will replace the closed Halbrook foundry.
